note: 'Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married ... Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” they said. “Does He not also speak through us?' (Num 12:1-2). **Two complaints in two verses** -- the marriage, then the standing -- and the chapter answers only the second.
'Now Korah ... Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab ... came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, You have taken too much upon yourselves!' (Num 16:1-3).

'Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes' (Num 14:6). **The two who brought back the minority report**, and the only two of that generation the Lord says will enter (14:30).
'All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron' (Num 14:2), and again with Korah's company: 'You have taken too much upon yourselves' (16:3).
'Now Korah ... Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab ... came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, You have taken too much upon yourselves' (Num 16:1-3).
'But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land' (Num 14:24).

note: 'Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them' (Num 20:12). **The whole of why he dies in Moab looking at it**, in one verse.
'Why then were you unafraid to speak against My servant Moses?' (Num 12:8), and Miriam becomes leprous, white as snow (12:10). **Only she is struck**, though the complaint was made by both.
'Now Korah ... Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab ... came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, You have taken too much upon yourselves!' (Num 16:1-3).

'From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh' (Num 13:6), among the twelve sent to search the land at 13:2.

'These were the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land; and Moses gave to Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua' (Num 13:16). **The renaming is recorded in the same verse as the sending**, which is the kind of aside the alias detector exists to find.
'Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock? Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff' (Num 20:10-11).
